pages.text: $(italic)$(#6b5a45)A building pack is simply a directory. Create $(#8a5a2b)data/<namespace>/buildings/<pack name>/$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) and drop building JSON into it and they belong to that pack;$(br) add a $(#8a5a2b)building_pack.json$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) inside and the pack gets a name and an icon.$()

Once a town has many buildings, one flat list stops being readable. A pack is the unit that groups buildings, ships them as a set, and keeps two authors' same-named buildings from colliding$(br) — inside one pack, ids only have to be unique within that pack.

$(#8a5a2b)buildings/cottage.json$() — a building sitting directly under $(#8a5a2b)buildings/$() belongs to the $(#8a5a2b)default$() pack$(li)$(#8a5a2b)buildings/medieval/inn.json$() — the directory name $(#8a5a2b)medieval$() is the pack name$(li)$(#8a5a2b)buildings/medieval/building_pack.json$() — this pack's metadata
pages.title: The Directory Is the Pack

pages.text: $(#8a5a2b)buildings/medieval/tower/watchtower.json$() — deeper nesting is only file organisation, still the $(#8a5a2b)medieval$() pack$(li)$(#8a5a2b)buildings/oriental/tea_house.json$() — a different pack$(br2)Only the $(bold)first$() level of subdirectories under $(#8a5a2b)buildings/$() names a pack; going deeper is tidying, not membership.
A building JSON may also carry a $(#8a5a2b)package_id$() field of its own, which $(bold)outranks the directory$(). Writing $(#8a5a2b)default$() there is the same as leaving it out, since it
pages.title: Naming One File's Pack

pages.text: falls back to the directory — the field is for pulling one file out of its folder, nothing more.$(br2)$(bold)Pack Metadata$()
$(#8a5a2b)building_pack.json$() sits in the pack directory, and every key in it may be omitted:$(br2)$(bold)Key  Default$()$(li)id — the directory name
name — the pack id$(li)description — empty$(li)author — empty$(li)version — $(#8a5a2b)1.0.0$()$(li)icon — $(#8a5a2b)minecraft:stone_bricks$()$(li)priority — 100

$(#8a5a2b)name$() takes either a literal string or a language key — both go through the same "use the lookup if it resolves, otherwise use the text as written" path, so a plain name is perf$(br)ectly legal and you need not invent a $(#8a5a2b)wandscape.pack.*$() key.
pages.title: Name and Ordering

pages.text: $(bold)The Default Pack$()$(br2)Every building the mod ships lives at the root and belongs to a pack called $(#8a5a2b)default$(), displayed as Core Pack.$(br2)$(#8a5a2b)icon$() takes an item id. The lower the $(#8a5a2b)priority$(), the earlier the pack sorts, and the mod's own core pack sits at 0.

$(bold)A $(#8a5a2b)buildings/building_pack.json$()$(bold) in any namespace is taken as that default pack's metadata$() — to write your own pack's $(#8a5a2b)building_pack.json$(), put it inside the pack directory;$(br) one at the root renames the default pack instead.

A directory with no $(#8a5a2b)building_pack.json$() is not an error;$(br) a placeholder pack is created, named after the directory. Writing a $(#8a5a2b)building_pack.json$() whose $(#8a5a2b)id$() differs from its directory name leaves the pack list calling it on
pages.title: When the Directory and the Id Disagree

pages.text: e thing while its buildings hang off another, matching neither.$(br2)$(bold)Can Players Switch a Pack Off$()

Yes. The Settings Center has a Pack Library page that disables a whole pack. Disabling only affects what the build list shows — buildings already standing in the world keep working and keep$(br) paying out. It is there for players tidying a list, not for pack authors to gate features with.

The Creative Building Scanner has a target-pack field;$(br) type a name that does not exist yet and the export creates that directory and writes a $(#8a5a2b)building_pack.json$() skeleton into it, recording you as the author. The pack name is lower
pages.title: Working With the Scanner

pages.text: cased, so $(#8a5a2b)Medieval$() and $(#8a5a2b)medieval$() are one and the same pack.$(br2)A scanner export goes into the save's own datapack under $(#8a5a2b)data/wandscape/buildings/<pack name>/$() — the pack and the namespace are two separate things, and an exported file always$(br) sits in the $(#8a5a2b)wandscape$() namespace.
